facts: A major axis of research at LIMSI is directed at multilingual, speaker-independent, large vocabulary speech dictation.
The paper describes the LIMSI recognizer.
The LIMSI recognizer was evaluated in the ARPA NOV93 CSR test.
The paper reports experimental results on the WSJ and BREF corpora under closely matched conditions.
For both corpora, word recognition experiments were carried out with vocabularies containing up to 20k words.
The recognizer makes use of continuous density HMM with Gaussian mixture for acoustic modeling.
The recognizer uses n-gram statistics estimated on the newspaper texts for language modeling.
The recognizer uses a time-synchronous graph-search strategy.
The time-synchronous graph-search strategy is shown to still be viable with a 20k-word vocabulary when used with bigram back-off language models.
A second forward pass makes use of a word graph generated with the bigram.
The second forward pass incorporates a trigram language model.
Acoustic modeling uses context-dependent phone models (intra and interword).
Acoustic modeling uses phone duration models.
